claim: For the canonical Sprott B flow \(\dot x=yz,\ \dot y=x-y,\ \dot z=1-xy\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\int xy\,d\mu=\int y^2\,d\mu=1\) and \(\int y^2z\,d\mu=-\int (x-y)^2\,d\mu\le 0\). Equality in the last identity holds exactly for convex mixtures of the equilibria \((1,1,0)\) and \((-1,-1,0)\). Consequently every other compact invariant probability measure gives positive mass to each of \(\{|y|<1\}\), \(\{|y|>1\}\), and \(\{z<0\}\); in particular every nonconstant periodic orbit crosses both sides of the equilibrium amplitude \(|y|=1\) and enters negative height.

correctness.rationale: The claim follows from the exact Lie derivatives \(Lz=1-xy\), \(L(y^2/2)=xy-y^2\), and \(L(xy)=x^2-xy+y^2z\). Invariant integration yields the two unit moments and the defect. The equality case was separately checked using invariance of compact support, which reduces \(x=y\) to the two equilibria.

value.rationale: The exact \(y\)-RMS locking is a natural global statistic of a canonical chaotic benchmark and is tied to the equilibrium amplitude rather than an arbitrary slice. Rigidity turns it into a strict two-sided amplitude excursion for every non-equilibrium invariant state, while the exact weighted-height defect forces negative-height recurrence. The result applies simultaneously to periodic and compact chaotic invariant measures.
